title: MatMul tutorial fails for float32 inputs
body:
I've ran the [3rd tutorial on matrix multiplication](https://triton-lang.org/main/getting-started/tutorials/03-matrix-multiplication.html#final-result) and the code runs successfully with the following versions
```
torch==2.0.0+cu118
triton==2.0.0
```

I then changed the dtypes of the input from half precision to single precision like below
```
a = torch.randn((512, 512), device='cuda', dtype=torch.float32)
b = torch.randn((512, 512), device='cuda', dtype=torch.float32)
```
Running this code then produces the output
```❌ Triton and Torch differ```

Why would making the inputs _higher_ precision cause worse numerical error in the output? I've been observing this on other kernels which was how I ended up trying it on the tutorial as well.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Tried upgrading to `triton==2.0.0post1` and moving the inputs to `torch.float32` causes the following error
```
TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'tuple' and 'float'
```

Going back to `torch.float16` it passes the test

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
It could be because TF32 is used (depending on what GPU you are using).
You can try adding `allow_tf32=False` to the dot operation.
By default torch won't use TF32, you can try to turn on TF32 in torch as well and compare.

> matrix size 512? seems still fine.
Do you mean that you don't observe the failures on float32 with matrix size 512?

> Can you increase the matrix size a bit?
I would think this would make it only _more_ likely to fail as the accumulation dimension gets larger. In any case, I've retried with 1024 and did the same three experiments with triton==2.1.0 and cuda 2.1.0

- ✅ Triton and Torch match tensor(0., device='cuda:0', dtype=torch.float16)
- ❌ Triton and Torch differ tensor(0.1706, device='cuda:0')
- ❌ Triton and Torch differ tensor(0.1889, device='cuda:0')

Looks like even the float32 without `allow_tf32` has pretty high absolute error. I understand there's some discrepancies expected due to non-associativity of floating point maths but the fact it's an exact match in f16 and not f32 was unexpected.

The output values are only on the order of 50 or so which wouldn't seem quite large enough for floating point errors to cause this big a difference

```

--- a/python/tutorials/03-matrix-multiplication.py
+++ b/python/tutorials/03-matrix-multiplication.py
@@ -233,7 +233,7 @@ def matmul_kernel(
         a = tl.load(a_ptrs, mask=offs_k[None, :] < K - k * BLOCK_SIZE_K, other=0.0)
         b = tl.load(b_ptrs, mask=offs_k[:, None] < K - k * BLOCK_SIZE_K, other=0.0)
         # We accumulate along the K dimension.
-        accumulator += tl.dot(a, b)
+        accumulator += tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=False)
         # Advance the ptrs to the next K block.
         a_ptrs += BLOCK_SIZE_K * stride_ak
         b_ptrs += BLOCK_SIZE_K * stride_bk
@@ -241,7 +241,7 @@ def matmul_kernel(

     if ACTIVATION == "leaky_relu":
         accumulator = leaky_relu(accumulator)
-    c = accumulator.to(tl.float16)
+    c = accumulator.to(tl.float32)

     # Write back the block of the output matrix C with masks.
@@ -295,8 +295,8 @@ def matmul(a, b, activation=""):

 torch.manual_seed(0)
-a = torch.randn((512, 512), device='cuda', dtype=torch.float16)

@@ -336,8 +336,8 @@ else:
     )
 )
